assumptions.original: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure. The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures. The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The drift coordinates are strongly progressive with almost surely continuous paths on [0,T]. The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.
assumptions.reconstructed: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). Each A_i is strongly progressive and has continuous paths on [0,T] mu-a.e.; no bounded-variation hypothesis. K is compact, fallback∈K, f is ambient C¹ at each point of K. Range inclusion holds mu-a.e. simultaneously for all t≤T.
assumptions.evidence: Full-module binder and definition audit: hAp requires progressive A and hAc only continuous paths, not BV. The local MeasurableSpace Omega := filtration t and hcut preserve the progressive domain. Fallback is merely measurable globally; continuity follows only on the confinement event; compactness gives the pointwise bound.

conclusion.original: Take actual completed Euclidean Itô rows with strongly progressive drifts and almost surely continuous drift paths. Evaluate the test derivative on a coordinate basis vector at the time-clipped state, using the fallback when the state is outside K. The weight is strongly progressive, almost surely continuous on the horizon and bounded there by a deterministic constant. Formula: W_i(t)=Df(\widetilde X_{\min(t,T)})[e_i],\qquad |W_i(t)|\le C_i\quad(0\le t\le T).
conclusion.reconstructed: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Set X_k(t)=A_k(t)+∑_j I_j(eta_kj)(t) and W(t,omega)=Df(inclusion(r(X(min(t,T),omega))))[e_i]. Then W is strongly progressive for F; mu-a.e. omega, W(·,omega) is continuous on [0,T]; and there exists C∈R such that for every t≤T and every omega, |W(t,omega)|≤C.
